newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas rises in Q4/Q1 but other periods quiet.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas rises in Q4/Q1 but other periods quiet.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw prices rising in the winter on Wednesday, with busy trade in the fourth quarter of this year, traders and brokers said.
But the market was otherwise quiet with prices little changed and few deals seen in other periods, dealers added.
The Q4 price went up quickly in the afternoon, trading as high as 13.20 pence before slipping back slightly.
"It was just hyped up by a couple of people this afternoon which is why it's short-lived. It went up quickly but then turned round straight away," said a trader.
Q4 was offered at 13.20 pence by the close and bid at 13.10 pence.
Another trader said he believed there is still room for the winter to go higher. "Q1 has still got a smidgeon to go. We might see it push above 17," he said.
"I think Q4 is still good value for buyers and may possibly come up. It's good for 13.5 pence, I think," he added.
The market was described as dead in the morning, but then took off when the IPE futures contract started trading in the afternoon.
It was not clear whether futures were leading the OTC market or the other way round, but at least one dealer said he felt the futures screen was leading the price.
"I felt I was watching the screen rather than listening too much to what was happening on the OTC," he said.
As well as a string of Q4 trades, there was also some activity on the Q1 98 market and some volumes done on the Q4/Q1 strip.
There were rumours that this had traded as high as 15.00 pence a therm, although this was not confirmed.
Apart from the winter the market was unusually quiet, with small volumes traded in the prompt period but no other periods coming in for serious discussion.
IPE futures saw 275 lots traded, nearly all at higher prices, and with all trade done between October and February - corresponding to the Q4/Q1 focus of the OTC market.
